plan.G: When research closes, retrieve each tree’s measured evidence and code. Compare only correctly validated programs using the official geometric-mean kernel-time objective; treat search measurements as provisional. Integrate evidence-backed changes incrementally, since combinations may be slower, and compile and check every combination afresh. Do not restart research or alter the protocol. Independently confirm the final candidate and retain the best independently confirmed program.
plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the supplied kernel has an O(N²) pair loop, so three distinct investigations can target source reuse within a CTA, register reuse across multiple targets, and arithmetic reduction. These are complementary implementation avenues rather than a fixed quota. The supplied baseline is valid and has mean_seconds 0.0018473421 across its three timing repetitions; no per-size breakdown or optimized-candidate measurements are available, so it is only an anchor, not evidence of a particular bottleneck. Require each tree to change only src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json, preserve the fixed interface and all-input correctness requirements, and judge candidates by the official correctness checks and geometric mean time for N=4096, 8192, and 16384.

children.objective: Investigate conventional shared-memory source tiling: cooperatively stage source particle data in chunks, synchronize correctly, and have CTA targets reuse each chunk while accumulating one output per thread. Explore tile and compatible launch configurations; handle partial tiles, self-interaction exclusion, and complete output coverage for all supported N. Do not make multi-target-per-thread coarsening the focus. Preserve the fixed interface, exact masses, and numerical tolerance; evaluate with the full correctness suite and official timing metric.
children.subject: CTA shared-memory source tiling

children.objective: Investigate target-axis register reuse by having each thread accumulate forces for multiple output particles, reusing each streamed source particle across those targets. Explore coarsening factors and compatible launch settings while monitoring register pressure and occupancy. Keep this path distinct from shared-memory source staging; ensure all outputs are covered for arbitrary N. Preserve the fixed interface, exact masses, and numerical tolerance; evaluate with the full correctness suite and official timing metric.
children.subject: Per-thread multi-target coarsening

children.objective: Investigate arithmetic and instruction-count reductions in a one-output-per-thread kernel without introducing shared-memory source tiling or multi-target coarsening. Evaluate algebraically equivalent force/acceleration factoring and reciprocal-distance formulations using available CUDA math operations, retaining adequate float32 accuracy without relying on a global fast-math option. Reject any variant that fails edge cases, the independent oracle, or tolerance. Measure against the official geometric-mean objective.

decision.rationale: Read the complete kernel source for the fastest supplied valid candidate before selecting an integration; the evidence reports 128 threads and a 256-entry shared tile.

Use the fastest supplied valid base: the shared-memory 256-source tile candidate (0.0008920 s versus baseline 0.0018473 s). Adapt the inverse-distance-cube correction from the separately measured, correct arithmetic trial (0.0012955 s): compute r=rsqrtf(distSq), e=fmaf(distSq,r*r,-1.0f), and use (r*r*r)*fmaf(-1.5f,e,1.0f) for the inverse cube. Guard r==0 before computing e so infinite distSq cannot produce NaN. Apply this to the original mass numerator; do not also cancel target mass or alter tiling, synchronization, self-exclusion, or integration. Keep the base launch configuration unchanged. Recompile and run the full correctness suite and official timing; the combination is unmeasured.

The first integration is correct and improved mean time to 0.0006500 s. Search the next diverse archive page for other measured, compatible transformations before choosing whether another combination is worthwhile.

model_interpretation.claim: Keeping one target per thread and a 128-thread CTA while doubling the source tile from 256 to 512 should halve the tile-loop and barrier-pair count for each target block. The tradeoff is twice the shared-memory footprint (8 KiB) and four cooperative loads per thread per tile, so official timing must determine whether the reduced synchronization overhead helps.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/launch.json","src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Changed the launch to 128 threads/targets per CTA with 8192 bytes of dynamic shared memory for 512 compact source records.","Cooperatively staged bounded source chunks and synchronized before use and before replacing each chunk, with inactive tail threads participating in barriers.","Kept one target and force accumulator per active thread, skipped self-interactions by global index, preserved the force and integration expressions, and guarded partial tiles and target tails."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Mapping three targets to each thread should reuse each streamed source particle across three independent force accumulations. A 128-thread block keeps 384 logical outputs per block, matching the selected factor-two parent's tile size while testing a different coarsening factor. The additional accumulators may increase register pressure and reduce occupancy; prior factor-two candidates were slower than baseline and the measured factor-four candidate was slower still, so no speedup is assumed.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/launch.json","src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Assign three output targets per thread at offsets 0, blockDim.x, and 2*blockDim.x, with separate force accumulators and self-interaction checks.","Load each source particle once per source-loop iteration and reuse its position and mass across valid targets; do not stage sources in shared memory.","Use 128 threads and 384 logical outputs per block, matching the parent tile size while changing the coarsening factor; bounds-check all targets to cover arbitrary N and final partial blocks."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Correct the inverse-distance cube directly using the squared relative error of rsqrtf, rather than refining the reciprocal distance and then cubing it. The first-order cube correction should have only a second-order residual when the rsqrt estimate is close, while reducing dependent multiplies. The controller must validate float32 tolerance and measure the official geometric-mean objective.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Form the unrefined inverse-distance cube as invDistSq * invDist.","Compute q - 1 with fmaf(distSq, invDistSq, -1.0f) and apply the first-order cube correction with fmaf(-1.5f, squareError, 1.0f).","Retain the zero-reciprocal guard so infinite squared distances do not create an infinity-times-zero NaN during correction."]}

model_interpretation.applicability: When reusing the T1 shared-memory approach, keep its validated 128-thread, 256-source configuration unless a new candidate is independently checked.
model_interpretation.claim: The supplied 256-source tiled candidate was valid at 0.0008920 s, while the supplied 512- and 1024-source tile attempts failed protected correctness checks; tile-size scaling cannot be assumed safe.
model_interpretation.next_experiment: Check this arithmetic integration against the full suite and official timing before considering any further tile changes.

model_interpretation.claim: With the existing 128-thread CTA, increasing the source tile from 512 to 1024 lets each CTA process twice as many sources per tile iteration, potentially reducing synchronization and loop overhead. The tradeoff is doubling dynamic shared memory from 8 KiB to 16 KiB and staging eight sources per thread; the controller's full correctness suite and official timing will determine whether this helps.

decision.rationale: The archive page shows the factor-two and factor-three coarsening candidates are slower than the integrated result, while larger T1 tiles failed correctness. Inspect the next diverse archive page for any other measured compatible idea before deciding whether to finish.

model_interpretation.claim: Keeping the target-mass force accumulation and final division avoids the accuracy risk of factoring target mass out of the pair loop. A Newton refinement of rsqrtf uses a previously validated CUDA formulation; the two ascending source ranges skip the self interaction without a per-pair self test. The split-loop code duplication may offset the saved branch, so correctness and the official geometric-mean objective must be measured by the controller.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Retain force accumulation with target mass in each pair contribution and divide accumulated force by target mass after the loop.","Use rsqrtf followed by one guarded Newton refinement to improve reciprocal-square-root accuracy without global fast math.","Traverse j < i and j > i in ascending order to skip the self interaction without a per-pair self comparison."]}

model_interpretation.applicability: Interpret the arithmetic correction as a candidate transformation, not as a guarantee of improving the faster tiled program.

decision.rationale: Try adapting only the self-branch avoidance from the correct T3 trial: for the tile containing an active target, accumulate indices before its local index and then after it; for other tiles, accumulate the full range. This preserves ascending source order and excludes self-interaction, avoiding unsafe evaluation of a potentially overflowing self-force. Retain the current corrected inverse-cube math and 128-thread/256-source tile. The T3 trial itself was slower (0.001248 s) than this valid base (0.000650 s), so its Newton refinement is not included; this is a bounded experiment, not an assumed improvement. Recheck and measure the full candidate, retaining the current best if it regresses.
